79731.subject: 🕵️ Two massive crypto hacks
79731.body:
———————————————————————————

## Top Stories

**BTC** $84,585 (1.3%) | **ETH** $2,720 (2.8%) | **SOL** $120 (6.2%)

* Bitget confirms hack with roughly [$350M](https://x.com/TreeNewsFeed/status/2103236015456457124) in losses, CEO says user funds are safe — [North Korean hackers](https://x.com/Cointelegraph/status/2103296178825633813) may be behind breach

* Yuga Labs VP 0xQuit [whitehats 23,155 NFTs](https://x.com/0xQuit/status/2103413056810439006) worth over $5.7M from Limit Break Payment Processor V2 exploit — [660 WETH](https://x.com/WuBlockchain/status/2103415730876383617) left unrecovered

* Crypto market rallies led by [ENA](https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/ethena/), [NEAR](https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/near-protocol/), and [LINK](https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/chainlink/)

* 10-year Treasury yield hits [5.10%](https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2102869384309964983), highest since 2007

* Long-dated US Treasury yields climb to highest level in [more than two decades](https://x.com/business/status/2103060137665605864)

* KelpDAO files civil claim against LayerZero and CEO Bryan Pellegrino over [$292M](https://x.com/WuBlockchain/status/2103354208452051303) exploit

* New York [sues Polymarket](https://x.com/TreeNewsFeed/status/2103127175595430364) over alleged gambling law violations, Kalshi faces similar allegations

* Cathie Wood's ARK Invest partners with Securitize to tokenize [ARK Venture Fund](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/09/24/cathie-wood-s-ark-teams-with-securitize-to-tokenize-venture-fund-with-openai-anthropic-stakes) on Ethereum

* Federal Reserve proposes regulatory framework for stablecoin issuers under the [GENIUS Act](https://x.com/WatcherGuru/status/2103191046012514681)

* 21Shares launches physically backed [Zcash and ETHFI ETPs](https://x.com/TheBlockCo/status/2102330614355562697) on Euronext Amsterdam and Paris

* Anthropic seeks shareholder approval for structure giving founders [50.1%](https://x.com/wallstengine/status/2103242264906768452) voting power ahead of IPO

* SoftBank kicks off junk bond sale targeting over [$11 billion](https://x.com/AGTPinsights/status/2102593975614115869) to fund AI investments

* Nearly [$16 billion](https://x.com/analyticsinme/status/2103099635632099838) in Bitcoin options expire today with major strikes at $90,000 and $100,000

* TokenWorks delivers FWA V2 [airdrop tokens](https://x.com/Rhynotic/status/2103269957278789863) to snapshot depositors — BitMON by Des Lucréce[ launches](https://x.com/token_works/status/2103182705844527451) on Fake World Assets October 1

🧠 Crypto News Brief: A $351.6M Bitget breach dominates the tape, yet markets stay calm with BTC near $85K after a record options expiry, while US regulators quietly advance stablecoin and derivatives rulebooks. 🚨 Bitget Loses $351.6M in Hot-Wallet Hack, Withdrawals Frozen Attackers breached a backend system in Bitget's wallet infrastructure on Sept. 24, spoofed transaction data and tricked the exchange's authorization process into releasing funds from hot and warm wallets. CEO Gracy Chen says private keys and cold storage were not compromised, withdrawals are paused pending review, and the $464M+ User Protection Fund will cover the full loss. Read full story 🎲 New York Sues Polymarket as Illegal Gambling, Polymarket Countersues Attorney General Letitia James and Gov. Kathy Hochul sued Polymarket US, alleging its event contracts are unlicensed gambling open to 18-year-olds, and seek to block it in the state plus penalties of up to three times alleged gains. Polymarket hit back hours later with a federal suit, arguing its CFTC-regulated exchange is outside state reach. More details 🏛️ Fed Unveils First GENIUS Act Rules for Stablecoin Issuers The Federal Reserve opened two proposals for comment: one requires Fed-supervised issuers to fully back tokens with short-term T-bills and other high-quality liquid assets, plus capital, risk and custody standards; the other sets an application process for banks seeking to issue stablecoins. A 60-day comment window starts on Federal Register publication. Read more ⚖️ CFTC Updates Crypto FAQs: Stablecoins as Margin, 20% Charge on BTC and ETH CFTC staff expanded guidance for futures firms and clearinghouses, confirming customer crypto can be used as margin, allowing proprietary payment stablecoins as residual interest with a 2% capital charge, and setting a 20% charge on BTC and ETH positions in line with SEC standards. Crypto remains barred as margin for uncleared swaps. See details 🏦 IBM Plugs Banks Into Swift's Blockchain Ledger for Tokenized Deposits IBM launched a beta adapter letting Digital Asset Haven clients instruct tokenized-deposit transfers on Swift's shared ledger using standard ISO 20022 payment messages, enabling round-the-clock movement before final settlement via existing systems. 79725.subject: When America walks away
79725.body:
The Economist Picks

Автор: The Economist


Автор: The Economist

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/when-america-walks-away-the-economist-x65ye?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BDFiQ1KNAQwWHA8iMcM%2FvIw%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2C69bl83dfjIs1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mugv6s5a~1o-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mugv6s5a-1o
  
Enjoying this newsletter? Get it in your inbox every Thursday, as well as our bonus weekend round-up of The Economist’s best journalism, by signing up for free here. I should have been more sceptical when a warrior waving a Barbie doll heaped praise on America. It was back in 2004, when the world was in awe of American firepower. George W. Bush had toppled tyrannies in Afghanistan and Iraq with televised ease. Saddam Hussein had been captured skulking in a spider hole. Fearing the same fate, Libya’s dictator, Muammar Qaddafi, had given up his nuclear-weapons programme.  For a while, the sense that America was invincible made diplomacy simpler. The White House told the warring parties in Sudan to make peace—or else—so they promptly started talking. Our reporter in southern Sudan, more than 3,000km from Baghdad, met a delighted young warrior who held up a Barbie doll and shouted: “This is a new wife for President Bush! May God grant him many fertile women with firm bodies and an election victory without problems in Florida!”  Yet prestige is fragile. That young fighter’s shoutout for an omnipotent America roughly coincided with the peak of its geopolitical pre-eminence. The country soon got bogged down in Iraq, unable to impose liberal democracy at gunpoint. Across the Arab world, where America had tried to shape a new order, revolutions, civil wars and jihadists raged. American presidents started to lose credibility. Barack Obama drew a “red line” in Syria and did nothing when a despot crossed it. Donald Trump makes so many empty threats—including another one this week to “annihilate” Iran—that people have given up counting.  Now, as Mr Trump seeks a way out of his ill-planned war, something momentous is occurring. As we describe in our cover package, American hegemony in the Middle East is ending. This is not just because its interventions raise oil prices, spurring American voters to punish the party in power. It is also because Americans are tired of the effort and expense of policing an explosive region, not very effectively. As Uncle Sam walks away, no one is poised to take his place, least of all any Arab state.
